newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle firm late, close mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle firm late, close mixed.

text.p: CME live cattle futures firmed again late to close mixed with nearbys up on ideas cash beef is bottoming. Feeder cattle closed higher as most grain futures were lower to limit down, traders said.
Live cattle closed 0.375 cent higher to 0.125 lower with April up most at 69.075 cents. Feeder cattle ended up 0.675 to 0.075 with May up 0.450 at 68.600 cents.

Live cattle slipped from early short covering gains when the stock market broke, but firmed again late as expectations continued for bottoming action in cash beef. Firmer beef should prompt packer interest for fed cattle, traders said.
Heavy-weight choice beef firmed Friday and again early Monday after falling more than $6 per cwt recently.

The active February marketing figure in the Cattle-on-Feed report, 99 percent of last year despite one less marketing day, added to nearby support. The strong marketing figure shows feedlots are very current and cattle marketings will likely not rise until summer, they said.
"(Feedlot) Supplies should be manageble for the next six weeks or so and then there's a little concern as we get into the summer," said Doug Harper, senior livestock analyst for Brock Associates Inc.

Lind-Waldock bought and locals covered shorts late with mixed market-on-close orders adding to April strength. R.J. O'Brien sold late morning but bought along with Refco. Refco also spread long June/short April. RBH sold, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, LFG was doing risk reversals, buying April 68 puts and selling 71 calls, pit sources added.

Feeder cattle traded higher much of day as most grain futures moved sharply lower. Although corn futures traded higher late, expectations are for corn to also move lower if other grains continue to slide, traders said.
"Feeders should continue to mirror corn," Harper said.
Traders also cited the overall firm tone to cash feeders. There has been good demand for feeders from both feedlots and for on-grass feeding, they said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.01 at $68.49 per cwt.
E.D.&F. Man sold before buying by Rosenthal Collins and LFG turned prices up. Cargill Investor Services spread long April/short May, pit sources said.
